title: Efficient Federated Search for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Lightweight Routing
shows: A small classifier picks which sources to query per question, cutting communication by up to 80.65% and latency by up to 52.50% with accuracy near querying every source.
takeaway: Put a cheap learned source router in front of live fetch so most questions touch only a few connected apps.

title: DFAMS: Dynamic-flow guided Federated Alignment based Multi-prototype Search
shows: Uses signals inside the LLM to detect query intent and route across heterogeneous knowledge partitions, beating prior federated retrieval by up to 6.45% in answer accuracy.
takeaway: Routing ambiguous cross-domain questions benefits from learned intent signals, so plan to train or tune the router on our own query logs.

title: Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Systematic Mapping Study
shows: Maps federated RAG work from 2020 to 2025 and flags privacy, client differences and weak evaluation as persistent open problems.
takeaway: Expect no ready benchmark for pointer-based federation; build our own evaluation covering source differences and privacy.

title: LiveVectorLake: A Real-Time Versioned Knowledge Base Architecture for Streaming Vector Updates and Temporal Retrieval
shows: Chunk-level hash change detection re-processed only about 10 to 15% of content per update on a small 100-document test, with a hot index and a versioned history store.
takeaway: Detect changes per chunk and keep a current tier plus version history; the test is tiny, so treat the numbers as a hint only.

title: From Static to Dynamic: A Streaming RAG Approach to Real-time Knowledge Base
shows: Keeps a compact set of prototype vectors refreshed during queries, reporting under 15 ms latency and over 900 documents per second within 150 MB.
takeaway: A small hot index can follow a change stream without blocking queries; verify on our own event volume before relying on it.

title: In-Place Updates of a Graph Index for Streaming Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
shows: Handles each insert and delete in place instead of batch consolidation, keeping recall stable over long update sequences.
takeaway: Choose a vector index that deletes in place, so removed or revoked documents leave search results quickly.

title: EMA: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with General Attribute Filtering and Dynamic Updates
shows: Filtered vector search over mixed numeric and categorical attributes with dynamic updates, reporting 1.68x to 12.25x speedup over general filtering methods.
takeaway: Permission, source and date filters can run inside updatable ANN search; benchmark this class of index for the pointer store.

title: From BM25 to Corrective RAG: Benchmarking Retrieval Strategies for Text-and-Table Documents
shows: On 23,088 financial queries, hybrid retrieval plus neural reranking was best (Recall@5 0.816), BM25 beat dense retrieval, and contextual retrieval gave steady gains.
takeaway: Ship hybrid lexical plus dense search with a reranker, and keep exact-match search for identifiers and numbers.

title: RECON: Benchmarking Agent Memory for Compositional Reasoning over Long Contexts
shows: A benchmark of 24 long case files where the best non-oracle system reaches only 22.4% accuracy at tracing how changed evidence affects conclusions.
takeaway: Retrieval alone will not handle changed facts that ripple downstream; add explicit supersession checks and test for them.

title: AgenticRAG: Agentic Retrieval for Enterprise Knowledge Bases
shows: An agent with search, find, open and summarize tools over existing enterprise search reports 92% correctness on FinanceBench, and tool use gave a 5.9x ablation gain.
takeaway: Expose the brain as a few simple tools an agent calls in a loop rather than one retrieval call.

title: Keyword search is all you need: Achieving RAG-Level Performance without vector databases using agentic tool use
shows: Agents with only keyword search tools reach over 90% of the performance of traditional RAG, with no persistent vector database.
takeaway: Live keyword calls to source APIs can be a strong baseline; test them against our index before paying for full embedding copies.

title: LiveMCPBench: Can Agents Navigate an Ocean of MCP Tools?
shows: On 95 tasks over 70 MCP servers and 527 tools, most models scored 30 to 50% success, and retrieval errors caused nearly half of failures.
takeaway: Picking the right connector tool is the bottleneck; keep a searchable catalog of tools and limit how many an agent sees.

title: MCP-Atlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Tool-Use Competency with Real MCP Servers
shows: 1,000 tasks over 36 real MCP servers; the best pass rate was 82.2%, and 63.3% of diagnosed failures were reasoning failures, not tool-call errors.
takeaway: Multi-server chaining fails mostly in planning, so the brain should return clear, structured results that make the next step obvious.

title: Benchmarking Deep Search over Heterogeneous Enterprise Data
shows: A benchmark over 39,190 artifacts from documents, transcripts, Slack and GitHub; the best agentic RAG method averages 32.96, with retrieval as the main bottleneck.
takeaway: Cross-app multi-hop questions are hard today; use this benchmark style, including unanswerable questions, as our acceptance test.

title: DRBench: A Realistic Benchmark for Enterprise Deep Research
shows: 100 open-ended tasks across 10 domains that need facts from both the public web and private email, chat and cloud files.
takeaway: Test the brain on report-style tasks that mix private and public sources, not just short factual questions.
